summary: Implement deterministic public OpenAPI-only Go, TypeScript and Python REST SDK generation, compatibility policy, examples and repository drift checks without exposing internal database models.

impacts.evidence: SDKs expose only public OpenAPI parameters and do not synthesize organization/workspace selectors; authenticated server-side scope remains authoritative.
Generated clients transport caller-provided public JSON only; generation rejects internal/database model tokens and does not copy SQL rows or private persistence fields.
All 29 current OpenAPI operationIds generate deterministically; API/SDK version policy and source SHA-256 manifest make drift and breaking generator changes reviewable.
Task 062 generates REST clients only and changes no event envelope or payload contract.
Connector Plugin SDK v1 remains unchanged; generated developer REST SDKs are a separate public surface.
No database schema, migration or persistence adapter changes are introduced.
Clients support bearer authentication but never persist credentials; generated/public trees are scanned for internal DB model leakage and use caller-injected transports for deterministic tests.
SDK generation does not authorize actions or bypass Task 017 approval policy; it only invokes the documented API surface.
Audit and lineage remain server-side behavior; clients do not duplicate or reinterpret those records.
Task 062 does not alter server idempotency/reconciliation semantics; generated clients preserve documented request paths and parameters.
Webhook management operations from Task 063 are represented in generated clients, but delivery signing/retry/SSRF logic stays server-side and is not duplicated.
No production SLO or telemetry semantics are claimed; SDK runtime behavior remains thin HTTP transport.
Generated artifacts are reproducible from the pinned OpenAPI source; rollback is restoring the previous OpenAPI/generator commit and regenerating exact artifacts.

sdk-check validates deterministic drift, generator tests, Go/TypeScript/Python client behavior, manifest/OpenAPI hash and operation parity, examples, and forbidden internal-model tokens. Architecture inventory explicitly admits only the generated Go SDK/example roots and sdkgen tool root while arbitrary sdk Go roots remain fail-closed.
